key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with optimized direct drive friction welding parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance from process settings.
engineering_relevance: The work offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive structures by pairing mechanical interlocking design with data-driven process optimization.
method: Used an L18 orthogonal array to study friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time.
Compared conventional flat-to-flat joints with a drilled-to-bossed geometry inspired by mortise-and-tenon interlocking.
Trained deep learning models, including an ensemble residual network, to predict ultimate tensile strength from welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The best condition reported 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the ensemble residual network achieved the strongest prediction performance with R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model accuracy is moderate rather than definitive, so broader validation on more weld conditions and repeatability tests would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
